Within-subscale item order is NOT verified against the data and cannot be. All four items ('Ethical', 'Respectable', 'Has integrity', 'Honest/upright') are near-synonymous adjectives on one 0-7 scale, and the paper publishes no per-item statistic (Table 2 is subscale x condition only). The 1->_1 .. 4->_4 assignment rests entirely on the S2 File's own numbered list under the heading 'Ethical:' matching the S3 File column suffixes mdmt_ethical_1..4, which are the IRW item codes verbatim. verification status is PARTIAL for this reason.

The study's Ethical subscale wording departs from the canonical MDMT. Ullman & Malle's MDMT v1 (2019-04-01) lists the Ethical subscale as 'ethical, respectable, principled, has integrity'; the S2 File lists 'Ethical, Respectable, Has integrity, Honest/upright'. Items 3 and 4 are therefore not the canonical items 3 and 4 -- 'Honest/upright' appears to be this study's Japanese-then-English rendering of 'principled'. Shipped as the study wrote it, not normalised to canonical wording.
